hypotheses.hypothesis: ClayCode needs explicit canonical IR/runtime lifetime state for opaque FFI resources so ownership transfer, borrowing, drop and kind identity are checked before host lowering.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Generic ResourceRef plus adapter-local conventions are sufficient; explicit lifetime state adds complexity without preventing additional failures.
evidence: WebAssembly Component Model WIT resource/own/borrow design
hypotheses.falsifier: A matched implementation using only generic ResourceRef achieves the same rejection coverage, deterministic replay and FFI correctness with lower complexity and no hidden adapter semantics.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The lifetime contract can remain canonical-IR/runtime semantics without adding first-class surface syntax such as own<T>/borrow<T> to ClayCode G9.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: First-class syntax is required for usable static diagnostics, generics and cross-dialect interop.
evidence: Current grammar can name distinct record types but does not encode linearity/borrowing directly.
hypotheses.falsifier: Compiler/application trials show that IR-only lifetime tracking causes ambiguous source diagnostics, unsafe lowering, or excessive annotation/repair cost.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Resource lifetime/ownership must remain orthogonal to capability/effect authority: owning a handle never self-authorizes an external effect.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: An owned handle may safely act as bearer authority for all operations on the resource.
hypotheses.falsifier: A host-enforced design demonstrates equivalent non-amplification, revocation, current-state revalidation and recovery while collapsing handle ownership and authority into one object.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Async/FFI borrowing requires dynamic or static task-scope lifetime enforcement so an owner cannot drop while a loan remains active and a borrow cannot escape its valid call/task scope.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Reference counting alone is sufficient and explicit borrow scopes are unnecessary.
evidence: WebAssembly Component Model concurrency borrow enforcement
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched async stress tests show reference-count-only semantics preserve ownership/drop/use invariants with equivalent diagnostics and lower overhead.

next_test: Integrate the candidate into a real ClayCode evaluator/FFI lowering slice, then differential-test owned/borrowed resource traces against a WebAssembly Component Model or equivalent reference backend on the Ubuntu target.
